<handoff-context>
## Goal
Integrate the real Intel DSA engine into the Prost resumable async payload-copy path so generated Prost `string` / `bytes` payload copies can offload through hardware while preserving byte-for-byte compatibility with synchronous `prost::Message::encode`.

## Constraints & Preferences
- Keep DSA opt-in; CPU encoding remains default.
- Do not modify `accel-rpc/tonic/tonic/src/codec/encode.rs`.
- Do not change Tonic codec plumbing unless required by compile break.
- `prost::Message::encode_raw` must remain synchronous.
- Use `AsyncEncodeSink::poll_put_payload` as the only generated-message payload-copy hook.
- No boxed futures in generated Prost hot path.
- No borrowed `BufMut`, `EncodeBuf`, or destination view may live across `Poll::Pending`.
- No staging `BytesMut` production copy path.
- Use existing DSA concepts where possible: `DsaConfig`, `SharedDsaWorkQueue`, `DsaWorkQueue`, `DsaMemmoveRetry`, `submit_retry`, `touch_pages_for_dsa`, completion polling, page-fault retry handling.
- Preserve existing fake offload E2E test.
- Hardware tests must be ignored and use `TONIC_DSA_WQ`, defaulting to `/dev/dsa/wq0.0`.

## Progress
### Done
- [x] Wrote project plan: `docs/plan/2026-06-10/04.prost-real-dsa-payload-copy.plan.md`.
- [x] Wrote agent plan: `agents/plan/2026-06-10/04.prost-real-dsa-payload-copy.plan.md`.
- [x] Inspected Prost async encode path:
  - `accel-rpc/tonic/prost/prost/src/transfer.rs`
  - `accel-rpc/tonic/prost/prost/src/encoding.rs`
  - `accel-rpc/tonic/prost/prost/src/message.rs`
  - `accel-rpc/tonic/prost/prost-derive/src/field/*`
  - `accel-rpc/tonic/prost/tests/src/message_encoding.rs`
- [x] Inspected existing DSA integration:
  - `accel-rpc/tonic/tonic-dsa-bytes-async/src/lib.rs`
  - `accel-rpc/tonic/tonic-dsa-bytes-async/src/prost_codec.rs`
  - `accel-rpc/tonic/tonic-dsa-bytes-sync/src/lib.rs`
  - `accel-rpc/tonic/tonic-dsa-bytes-sync/src/dsa_buf.rs`
- [x] Implemented/finalized real Prost DSA payload-copy path in `accel-rpc/tonic/tonic-dsa-bytes-async/src/prost_codec.rs`.
  - Main sink: `DsaProstEncodeSink`.
  - Hook: `impl AsyncEncodeSink for DsaProstEncodeSink::poll_put_payload`.
  - Payload state: `DsaProstPayloadState`.
  - Pending copy state: `PendingDsaProstPayloadCopy`.
  - Uses `DsaMemmoveRetry`, `submit_retry`, `touch_pages_for_dsa`.
  - CPU fallback path calls `self.buf.as_encode_buf().put_slice(payload)`.
  - DSA path reserves destination with `EncodeBuf::reserve_uninit_slice_for_pending`.
  - DSA success commits with `EncodeBuf::advance_reserved_uninit_slice`.
  - Drop path drains in-flight descriptor via `PendingDsaProstPayloadCopy::drain_completion`.
- [x] Fixed drop-order safety in `DsaAsyncProstEncode<T>` by declaring `state: PollEncodeState<DsaProstEncodeSink>` before `item: Option<T>` and `sink: Option<DsaProstEncodeSink>`, so pending descriptor state drains before source message or destination buffer owner drops.
- [x] Added/expanded ignored hardware test in `accel-rpc/tonic/tonic-dsa-bytes-async/tests/hardware_dsa.rs`.
  - New helper: `open_test_work_queue()`.
  - New generated Prost fixture structs:
    - `HardwareNestedPayload`
    - `HardwareProstMessage`
    - `HardwarePayloadOneof`
    - `HardwareNestedOneof`
  - New test: `dsa_work_queue_encodes_generated_prost_payload_shapes`.
  - Covers scalar, string, bytes, repeated string/bytes, map string/bytes, nested messages, repeated nested, map nested, bytes oneof, nested-message oneof.
  - Compares hardware-produced bytes against synchronous `msg.encode(&mut expected)`.
  - Decodes hardware-produced bytes with normal Prost decode and asserts equality.
  - Asserts at least one `Poll::Pending` occurred.
- [x] Ran formatter for async DSA crate:
  - From `accel-rpc/tonic`: `rtk cargo fmt -p tonic-dsa-bytes-async`
- [x] Verification from `accel-rpc/tonic/prost`:
  - `PROTOC_INCLUDE=/home/hongtao/accel-datapath/tonic-dsa/accel-rpc/tonic/prost/tests/src/include rtk cargo test -p tests async_encode`
  - Result: `7 passed, 62 filtered out`.
- [x] Full Prost verification from `accel-rpc/tonic/prost`:
  - `PROTOC_INCLUDE=/home/hongtao/accel-datapath/tonic-dsa/accel-rpc/tonic/prost/tests/src/include rtk cargo test -p prost -p prost-derive -p tests`
  - Result: `489 passed, 13 ignored`.
- [x] Async DSA crate verification from `accel-rpc/tonic`:
  - `rtk cargo test -p tonic-dsa-bytes-async`
  - Result: `7 passed, 2 ignored`.
- [x] Sync DSA crate verification from `accel-rpc/tonic`:
  - `rtk cargo test -p tonic-dsa-bytes-sync`
  - Result: `8 passed`.
- [x] Hardware test direct run failed without capability:
  - Command: `TONIC_DSA_WQ=/dev/dsa/wq0.0 PROTOC_INCLUDE=/home/hongtao/accel-datapath/tonic-dsa/accel-rpc/tonic/prost/tests/src/include rtk cargo test -p tonic-dsa-bytes-async --test hardware_dsa -- --ignored --nocapture`
  - Failure: `failed to open /dev/dsa/wq0.0: async dsa bytes encode failed to open /dev/dsa/wq0.0: Operation not permitted (os error 1)`.
- [x] Hardware verification succeeded through launcher:
  - Command from `accel-rpc/tonic`:
    `TONIC_DSA_WQ=/dev/dsa/wq0.0 PROTOC_INCLUDE=/home/hongtao/accel-datapath/tonic-dsa/accel-rpc/tonic/prost/tests/src/include rtk ../../tools/build/dsa_launcher cargo test -p tonic-dsa-bytes-async --test hardware_dsa -- --ignored --nocapture`
  - Result: `2 passed`.
- [x] Whitespace check:
  - From repo root: `rtk git diff --check`
  - Result: passed.
- [x] Audited forbidden Tonic codec file:
  - From `accel-rpc/tonic`: `rtk git diff --name-only -- tonic/src/codec/encode.rs && rtk git status --short -- tonic/src/codec/encode.rs`
  - Result: no diff; output included `ok`.

### In Progress
- [ ] None.

### Pending
- [ ] No required implementation or verification tasks remain.
- [ ] Optional: commit or review full workspace diff, because several files were already modified/untracked before/around this work.

## Key Decisions
- **Keep DSA behind `tonic-dsa-bytes-async`**: Hardware-specific work queue, descriptor, retry, page-touching, and completion logic stay in the experimental DSA crate rather than in upstream-shaped Prost APIs.
- **Use `AsyncEncodeSink::poll_put_payload` only**: Generated Prost code already calls this hook for `string` / `bytes` payload bytes after CPU-writing keys and lengths, so no additional Prost or Tonic codec hook was added.
- **CPU fallback remains default**: `DsaProstEncodeSink::selected_work_queue` returns `None` when no queue is configured or payload length is below `DsaConfig::min_message_bytes`, and fallback copies synchronously with `put_slice`.
- **Destination safety via pending reservation**: DSA path reserves uninitialized destination capacity with `reserve_uninit_slice_for_pending`, stores stable raw source/destination pointers in pinned payload state, and commits with `advance_reserved_uninit_slice` exactly once after DSA success.
- **Drop-order fix is required for soundness**: `DsaAsyncProstEncode<T>` now drops `state` before `item` and `sink`, ensuring an in-flight descriptor is drained before the source message or destination buffer can be released.
- **Use `BTreeMap` in hardware fixture**: Map fields in the hardware test use `#[prost(btree_map = ...)]` so synchronous expected bytes are deterministic for byte-for-byte comparison.

## Critical Context
- Core implementation file: `accel-rpc/tonic/tonic-dsa-bytes-async/src/prost_codec.rs`.
- Key symbols in `prost_codec.rs`:
  - `DsaAsyncProstCodec<T, U>`
  - `DsaAsyncProstEncoder<T>`
  - `DsaAsyncProstEncode<T>`
  - `DsaProstEncodeSink`
  - `DsaProstPayloadState`
  - `PendingDsaProstPayloadCopy`
  - `PendingYieldingProstPayloadCopy`
- `DsaAsyncProstEncode<T>` field order is intentional:
  ```rust
  pub struct DsaAsyncProstEncode<T> {
      // Drop order is part of the safety contract...
      state: PollEncodeState<DsaProstEncodeSink>,
      item: Option<T>,
      sink: Option<DsaProstEncodeSink>,
      options: EncodeOptions,
      stage: DsaAsyncProstEncodeStage,
  }
  ```
- DSA payload copy path in `PendingDsaProstPayloadCopy::poll`:
  - On first poll:
    - Gets `len = source.len()`.
    - Creates short-lived `let mut dst = buf.as_encode_buf();`.
    - Reserves destination with unsafe `dst.reserve_uninit_slice_for_pending(len)`.
    - Calls `touch_pages_for_dsa(source.as_ptr(), dst_ptr, len)`.
    - Builds `DsaMemmoveRetry::new(source.as_ptr(), dst_ptr, len)`.
    - Calls `submit_retry(&this.work_queue, &mut this.desc, &mut this.completion, &retry)`.
    - Stores `source`, `source_len`, `dst`, `dst_len`, `retry`, `submitted = true`.
  - While completion status is `DsaCompletionStatus::None.as_u8()`, wakes and returns `Poll::Pending`.
  - On `DsaRetryAction::Complete`, sets `completed = true` and advances reserved bytes once.
  - On `DsaRetryAction::Retry`, calls `submit_retry` again and returns `Pending`.
  - On error, marks completed and returns `Status`.
  - `Drop` calls `drain_completion`.
- Existing raw async DSA machinery in `accel-rpc/tonic/tonic-dsa-bytes-async/src/lib.rs` remains the model:
  - `DsaConfig`
  - `DsaWorkQueue`
  - `SharedDsaWorkQueue`
  - `DsaMemmoveRetry`
  - `DsaRetryAction`
  - `submit_retry`
  - `touch_pages_for_dsa`
- Hardware test file: `accel-rpc/tonic/tonic-dsa-bytes-async/tests/hardware_dsa.rs`.
- New hardware test requires capability; run through `../../tools/build/dsa_launcher` from `accel-rpc/tonic` if direct run gets EPERM.
- Observed direct hardware failure without launcher:
  `Operation not permitted (os error 1)`.
- Root repository status at handoff included many pre-existing/unrelated untracked paths. Do not revert them blindly.
- `accel-rpc/tonic` status after work:
  - Modified:
    - `Cargo.toml`
    - `release-plz.toml`
    - `tonic-dsa-bytes-async/Cargo.toml`
    - `tonic-dsa-bytes-async/src/lib.rs`
    - `tonic-dsa-bytes-async/tests/hardware_dsa.rs`
  - Untracked:
    - `prost/`
    - `tonic-dsa-bytes-async/src/prost_codec.rs`
    - `tonic-prost-async/`
- Important: `tonic-dsa-bytes-async/src/prost_codec.rs` appeared as untracked in final status even though it contains the real DSA Prost implementation and was edited. Ensure it is included if committing/reviewing.
- Plan files updated with completion notes:
  - `docs/plan/2026-06-10/04.prost-real-dsa-payload-copy.plan.md`
  - `agents/plan/2026-06-10/04.prost-real-dsa-payload-copy.plan.md`
- No changes under `accel-rpc/tonic/tonic/src/codec/encode.rs`.

## Next Steps
1. Review the full `accel-rpc/tonic` diff including untracked `tonic-dsa-bytes-async/src/prost_codec.rs`, `prost/`, and `tonic-prost-async/` before committing, because some workspace changes predated this session.
2. If preparing a commit, include the plan files and ensure the untracked implementation/test files are staged intentionally.
3. Preserve the exact verification commands/results above in the commit or report.
4. Do not rerun direct hardware tests without launcher unless the process has `CAP_SYS_RAWIO`; use `../../tools/build/dsa_launcher` from `accel-rpc/tonic`.

I need to focus on the user’s question about why the test folder is in "tonic-dsa-bytes-async." I think it might be a typo, but I should provide a technical answer. I wonder if they expect the hardware test to be outside the crate. In Rust, integration tests for a crate typically reside in the `tests/` directory within that crate. So, I want to explain that standard practice to clarify any confusion.

**Explaining test folder rationale**

The DSA hardware-specific test is in `tonic-dsa-bytes-async` for a few reasons. Firstly, the DSA implementation and public API are found there, not in prost or tonic. This setup keeps those crates hardware-agnostic. The test relies on the Linux DSA queue and can use ignored tests without affecting other prost tests. It also verifies integration with the generated Prost and DsaAsyncProstCodec. Lastly, we’re not putting it in `prost/tests` or `tonic/tests` as those should remain generic.

content.text:
Because it is the crate that owns the opt-in DSA behavior.

`tonic-dsa-bytes-async/tests/hardware_dsa.rs` is a Rust integration-test folder for that crate, not a generic Tonic/Prost test folder.

Why it belongs there:

- Real DSA queue setup lives in `tonic-dsa-bytes-async`.
- `DsaAsyncProstCodec` / `DsaProstEncodeSink` are crate-local DSA integration surfaces.
- Prost itself must stay hardware-agnostic and synchronous by default.
- Tonic codec plumbing was intentionally not changed.
- Hardware tests need `TONIC_DSA_WQ`, ignored test flags, and launcher/capability handling; keeping that inside the DSA crate avoids polluting normal Prost/Tonic tests.
- The test still exercises generated Prost messages end-to-end; it just uses the DSA crate as the opt-in adapter.

So the boundary is:

```text
prost/                      generic async encode hook + generated code support
tonic/                      unchanged codec plumbing
tonic-dsa-bytes-async/      real Intel DSA implementation + hardware tests
```

If we put the hardware test under `prost/tests`, Prost would start depending on DSA/Linux hardware concepts, which is the wrong dependency direction.

# accel-rpc AGENTS

Inherits `../AGENTS.md`.

## OVERVIEW
Rust workspace for accelerator-aware RPC components around Tonic, plus small benchmarking and profiling crates.

## WHERE TO LOOK
| Task | Location | Notes |
|------|----------|-------|
| Workspace membership | `Cargo.toml` | `tonic` is excluded even though it is present as a submodule. |
| Codec work | `accel-codec/` | Pooled-buffer codec crate. |
| Middleware work | `accel-middleware/` | Tower CRC/compression middleware. |
| Rust IDXD binding stack | `idxd-rust/` (safe) with repo-root `idxd-sys/` (raw) | Canonical DSA/IDXD bridge crates. |
| Async overhead bench | `async-bench/` | `cargo bench` is the real measurement path. |
| Profiling harness | `tonic-profile/` | Still marked TODO. |

## CONVENTIONS
- Treat this subtree as a workspace first: update the member crate and the workspace manifest together when boundaries change.
- Do not assume the vendored `tonic/` subtree is part of normal workspace edits; it is intentionally excluded.
- Keep commands Cargo-native unless a crate README says otherwise.

## ANTI-PATTERNS
- Do not present `tonic-profile` as production-ready; the current harness is a placeholder.
- Do not add crate-specific guidance here if the crate is still only a manifest plus stub source; keep the parent file thin until complexity grows.

## COMMANDS
```bash
cd accel-rpc && cargo build
cd accel-rpc && cargo check
cd accel-rpc && cargo bench -p async-bench
```

# Agent Notes

## Primary direction: DSA integration toward tonic

This workspace is for moving Intel DSA codec work toward tonic without turning
tonic into a hardware-specific fork.

- Keep `tonic` and `tonic-prost` upstream-shaped: generic codec APIs, stable
  call sites, and CPU behavior as the default path.
- Use `tonic-dsa-bytes-sync` as the current experimental DSA/bytes crate.
  Keep prost-specific DSA work aside until the raw byte/`Buf` codec boundary is
  proven useful.
- DSA paths must stay opt-in. Device paths, shared work queues, descriptor
  polling, and other `idxd` details belong behind the DSA crate boundary until a
  tonic-level abstraction is justified.
- Preserve the ordinary `tonic-prost` codec as the baseline. When changing codec
  hot paths, compare against the recorded benchmark baseline before claiming a
  performance win or no regression.
- Prefer clean cutovers once an abstraction is proven. Remove temporary shims,
  duplicated codec paths, and compatibility wrappers that no longer carry their
  weight.

## Codec performance checks

For async codec performance checks, use the recorded baseline file instead of
rerunning `origin/master` every time:

- Baseline file: `tonic/benches/decode-origin-master-4687108.bench`
- Benchmark command for the current branch: `cargo bench -p tonic --bench decode`

Workflow:
1. Run the benchmark on the current branch.
2. Compare the output to the recorded baseline file.
3. Rerun `origin/master` only when the benchmark file is stale, the benchmark
   changed, dependency resolution changed, or the run is on meaningfully
   different hardware/toolchain.

# docs AGENTS

Inherits `../AGENTS.md`.

## OVERVIEW
Documentation and knowledge-base inputs. This subtree is about document placement and retrieval semantics, not code execution.

## WHERE TO LOOK
| Task | Location | Notes |
|------|----------|-------|
| Plans | `plan/` | Human-readable project work plans. |
| Reports | `report/` | Findings and validation writeups. |
| Specs | `specs/README.md` | Authoritative local DSA/IAX specs. KB-tracked. |
| Related work | `related_work/README.md` | Thesis-driven note organization. |

## CONVENTIONS
- Keep project knowledge in tracked markdown under `docs/plan/`, `docs/report/`, or `docs/specs/`.
- Plan files under `docs/plan/` are human-readable project records. Write them so a project reviewer can understand the goal, scope, intended changes, verification, and outcome without needing agent-specific shorthand.
- Agent execution/workflow plans belong under `../agents/plan/`, not `docs/plan/`.
- For `docs/report/`, use topic directories and name files as `report/<topic>/NNN.<descriptor>.<ext>`; see `docs/report/AGENTS.md` for topic meanings. Agent-workflow reports belong under `../agents/report/workflow/`.
- Use `docs/related_work/` for curated topic notes tied to the repo thesis, not as the primary dump for searchable paper extraction.
- When a paper or PDF should become KB-searchable, extract or curate it into markdown under a tracked path, usually `docs/report/`.
- Keep single-point observations in `../remark/`; this file only narrows rules inside `docs/`.

## ANTI-PATTERNS
- Do not treat raw PDFs as KB inputs.
- Do not put spec facts into ad hoc notes when `docs/specs/` is the authoritative source.
- Do not duplicate root workflow rules for naming plans, reports, or remarks here.
- Do not write plan files as agent-only scratchpads or unexplained shorthand; even agent execution plans in `../agents/plan/` need a clear reader, scope, and verification.

# agents AGENTS

Inherits `../AGENTS.md`.

## OVERVIEW

This subtree is for agent-facing operating material: workflow reports, task-shaping notes, prompt/template rationale, and other durable guidance whose primary reader is a coding agent.

## PLACEMENT

- Use `plan/YYYY-MM-DD/NN.<topic>.<state>.md` for agent execution plans before non-trivial changes to agent operation, delegation, tooling, prompt templates, or live-thread workflow.
- Use `report/workflow/` for durable reports about agent orchestration, retrieval strategy, context budgeting, live-thread state, and process-level agent behavior.
- Keep domain research, architecture, benchmarking, hardware validation, literature synthesis, and specs in `../docs/`.
- Keep active executable agent assets in their established runtime locations unless a migration explicitly updates those consumers.

- Do not make normal Prost APIs require DSA, Tonic, device paths, or hardware capabilities.
- Hardware-backed DSA tests must stay ignored and opt in through `TONIC_DSA_WQ`.

# tonic-dsa-bytes-async AGENTS

Inherits `../AGENTS.md`.

## CRATE JOB
- Provide opt-in async Intel DSA byte-copy support for tonic encode paths.
- Keep the raw `Bytes` codec focused on copying payload bytes through DSA without protobuf-specific behavior.
- Keep DSA queue setup, descriptor submission, completion polling, and page-fault retry handling behind this crate boundary.

## TEST OWNERSHIP
- Raw bytes codec hardware smoke tests belong in this crate.
- Generated protobuf field-shape/e2e tests belong in `../prost/tests` and should exercise Prost's async payload-copy hook.

## Intended changes

- Add the generated-message DSA e2e hardware coverage to Prost tests.
- Add any test-only dependency wiring needed for Prost tests to call the opt-in DSA encoder.
- Keep Tonic codec plumbing unchanged.

- Raw bytes codec hardware smoke tests belong in this crate.
- Generated protobuf field-shape/e2e tests belong in `../prost/tests` and should exercise Prost's async payload-copy hook.

content.text:
Yes.

The hardware e2e test constructs one `HardwareProstMessage`:

```rust
let msg = HardwareProstMessage { ... };
```

Then:

1. Software path:
   ```rust
   msg.encode(&mut expected)
   ```

2. DSA path:
   ```rust
   tokio_stream::iter(std::iter::once(Ok::<_, Status>(msg.clone())))
   ```

3. It asserts byte-for-byte equality:
   ```rust
   assert_eq!(&data[HEADER_SIZE..], expected.as_slice());
   ```

4. It also decodes the DSA-produced bytes and checks semantic equality:
   ```rust
   let decoded = HardwareProstMessage::decode(&data[HEADER_SIZE..])?;
   assert_eq!(decoded, msg);
   ```

The DSA run uses `msg.clone()`, so it is the same logical protobuf message, not independently regenerated data. Maps use `BTreeMap`, so field ordering is deterministic for byte-for-byte comparison.

378:/// Engine that owns message transfer from a prost message into a destination.
379:///
380:/// The trait is intentionally separate from [`Message`], so generated structs
381:/// and existing synchronous call sites do not grow hardware-specific methods or
382:/// required async hooks.
383:pub trait EncodeEngine: Clone + Send + Sync + 'static {
384:    /// Error produced while starting or completing an encode operation.
385:    type Error: From<EncodeError> + Send + Sync + 'static;
386:
387:    /// Owned future returned for one encode operation.
388:    type Encode<M, B>: Future<Output = Result<B, Self::Error>> + Send + 'static
389:    where
390:        M: Message + Send + 'static,
391:        B: EncodeDst + Send + 'static;
392:
393:    /// Starts encoding `message` into owned destination `dst`.
394:    fn encode<M, B>(
395:        &self,
396:        message: M,
397:        dst: B,
398:        options: EncodeOptions,
399:    ) -> Result<Self::Encode<M, B>, Self::Error>
400:    where
401:        M: Message + Send + 'static,
402:        B: EncodeDst + Send + 'static;
403:}

405:/// CPU-backed encode engine using prost's existing synchronous [`Message`] API.
406:#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default)]
407:pub struct CpuEngine;
408:
409:/// Ready future returned by [`CpuEngine`].
410:#[derive(Debug)]
411:pub struct CpuEncode<B> {
412:    result: Option<Result<B, EncodeError>>,
413:}
414:
415:impl<B> CpuEncode<B> {
416:    #[inline]
417:    fn new(result: Result<B, EncodeError>) -> Self {
418:        Self {
419:            result: Some(result),
420:        }
421:    }
422:
423:    /// Consumes this ready future and returns the encoded destination.
424:    ///
425:    /// This is useful for adapters that must preserve a synchronous ready fast
426:    /// path while still routing encoding through [`EncodeEngine`].
427:    #[inline]
428:    pub fn into_result(mut self) -> Result<B, EncodeError> {
429:        self.result
430:            .take()
431:            .expect("CpuEncode polled or consumed after completion")
432:    }
433:}
434:
435:impl<B> Unpin for CpuEncode<B> {}
436:
437:impl<B> Future for CpuEncode<B> {
438:    type Output = Result<B, EncodeError>;
439:
440:    #[inline]
441:    fn poll(self: Pin<&mut Self>, _cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Self::Output> {
442:        Poll::Ready(
443:            self.get_mut()
444:                .result
445:                .take()
446:                .expect("CpuEncode polled after completion"),
447:        )
448:    }
449:}
450:
451:impl EncodeEngine for CpuEngine {
452:    type Error = EncodeError;
453:
454:    type Encode<M, B>
455:        = CpuEncode<B>
456:    where
457:        M: Message + Send + 'static,
458:        B: EncodeDst + Send + 'static;
459:
460:    #[inline]
461:    fn encode<M, B>(
462:        &self,
463:        message: M,
464:        mut dst: B,
465:        options: EncodeOptions,
466:    ) -> Result<Self::Encode<M, B>, Self::Error>
467:    where
468:        M: Message + Send + 'static,
469:        B: EncodeDst + Send + 'static,
470:    {
471:        let result = {
472:            let mut buf = dst.as_buf_mut();
473:            if options.length_delimited {
474:                message.encode_length_delimited(&mut buf)
475:            } else {
476:                message.encode(&mut buf)
477:            }
478:        };
479:
480:        Ok(CpuEncode::new(result.map(|()| dst)))
481:    }
482:}

# Prost DSA test ownership

## Goal
Move generated-Prost DSA payload-copy validation to the Prost test surface, and document the local crate responsibilities so future changes keep the dependency boundary clear.

## Scope
- Keep raw bytes DSA codec tests in `tonic-dsa-bytes-async`.
- Place generated protobuf encoding coverage under `prost/tests`.
- Add small crate-local `AGENTS.md` files for `prost/` and `tonic-dsa-bytes-async/`.
- Preserve opt-in hardware execution through the Prost `hardware-dsa` feature, ignored tests, and `TONIC_DSA_WQ`.

## Intended changes
- Remove generated-message shape coverage from the DSA bytes crate hardware test file.
- Add the generated-message DSA e2e hardware coverage to Prost tests.
- Add any test-only dependency wiring needed for Prost tests to call the opt-in DSA encoder.
- Keep Tonic codec plumbing unchanged.

## Verification
- Run the targeted Prost async/protobuf encoding tests.
- Run the async DSA crate tests to ensure raw bytes DSA coverage still passes.
- Run the ignored hardware protobuf encoding test through the DSA launcher when direct access is not permitted.

## Completion notes
Completed. Generated protobuf DSA hardware coverage now lives in `prost/tests/src/hardware_dsa.rs`; `tonic-dsa-bytes-async/tests/hardware_dsa.rs` keeps only the raw bytes codec hardware smoke test. Added crate-local AGENTS guidance for `prost/` and `tonic-dsa-bytes-async/`. Verified with targeted Prost async encode tests, the ignored DSA protobuf hardware test through `dsa_launcher`, async DSA crate tests, and `git diff --check`.

displayContent.text:
# Agent Notes

## Primary direction: DSA integration toward tonic

This workspace is for moving Intel DSA codec work toward tonic without turning
tonic into a hardware-specific fork.

- Keep `tonic` and `tonic-prost` upstream-shaped: generic codec APIs, stable
  call sites, and CPU behavior as the default path.
- Use `tonic-dsa-bytes-sync` as the current experimental DSA/bytes crate.
  Keep prost-specific DSA work aside until the raw byte/`Buf` codec boundary is
  proven useful.
- DSA paths must stay opt-in. Device paths, shared work queues, descriptor
  polling, and other `idxd` details belong behind the DSA crate boundary until a
  tonic-level abstraction is justified.
- Preserve the ordinary `tonic-prost` codec as the baseline. When changing codec
  hot paths, compare against the recorded benchmark baseline before claiming a
  performance win or no regression.
- Prefer clean cutovers once an abstraction is proven. Remove temporary shims,
  duplicated codec paths, and compatibility wrappers that no longer carry their
  weight.

## Codec performance checks

For async codec performance checks, use the recorded baseline file instead of
rerunning `origin/master` every time:

- Baseline file: `tonic/benches/decode-origin-master-4687108.bench`
- Benchmark command for the current branch: `cargo bench -p tonic --bench decode`

Workflow:
1. Run the benchmark on the current branch.
2. Compare the output to the recorded baseline file.
3. Rerun `origin/master` only when the benchmark file is stale, the benchmark
   changed, dependency resolution changed, or the run is on meaningfully
   different hardware/toolchain.

1:# PROJECT KNOWLEDGE BASE
2:
3:Research monorepo for Intel DSA/IAX data-path work.
4:
5:## CONVENTIONS
6:
7:- Keep durable detail in plans, reports, and remarks rather than transient notes.
8:- Keep commit headlines short and consistent with current style.
9:- Write commits in focused, reviewable increments, but not so small that they lose a coherent unit of work.
10:- Write a human project plan in `docs/plan/YYYY-MM-DD/NN.<topic>.<state>.md` before non-trivial project changes. State the goal, scope, intended changes, verification, and completion notes in plain language.
11:- Always write agent execution/workflow plans in `agents/plan/YYYY-MM-DD/NN.<topic>.<state>.md`.
12:- Write findings to `docs/report/<topic>/NNN.<descriptor>.<ext>`.
13:- Write single-point insights to `remark/NNN_<topic>.md`.
14:- Match code to specs, not specs to code, unless explicitly told otherwise.
15:- **Code Elegance & Lean Design:** Keep code lean. Do not repeat duplicate logic; abstract if possible, or keep it perfectly clean if unavoidable. If code looks heavyweight with excessive conditionals, stop and design a more elegant approach.
16:- Keep child `AGENTS.md` files lean and local; do not repeat parent guidance within them.
17:
18:## DO NOT
19:- Guess DSA/IAX behavior if `docs/specs/*.md` or `docs/report/architecture/001.design_decisions.md` already cover it.
20:- Run hardware-facing binaries directly when the documented flow requires `launch` or `dsa_launcher`.
21:
22:## HARDWARE BATCHING TERMINOLOGY
23:- Use `hw-eval/` as the hardware potential baseline when comparing accelerator submission strategies.
24:- Keep `batch` and `concurrency` separate in plans, reports, and code names.
25:- **Batch size (`batch_n`):** The number of logical operations submitted to hardware through one MMIO submission. Batch size 1 means one operation per MMIO submission.
26:- **Concurrency:** The maximum number of logical operations outstanding at once, independent of how those operations are grouped into MMIO submissions.
27:- If a benchmark reports outstanding submission slots instead of logical operations, convert before comparing:
28:  $$logical\_concurrency = batch\_size \times outstanding\_submission\_slots$$
29:- Avoid ambiguous phrases like “batch size 1” without specifying whether it means the no-batch/direct-descriptor baseline or a DSA `BATCH` descriptor containing one sub-descriptor.
30:- Keep hw-eval-specific strategy names and command-line trigger details in `hw-eval/AGENTS.md`.
31:
32:## REPO MAP
33:```text
34:dsa-stdexec/  C++ stdexec sender/receiver framework
35:accel-rpc/    Rust accelerator-aware RPC workspace
36:hw-eval/      Hardware potential baseline benchmark harnesses
37:docs/         Plans, reports, specs, related work
38:tools/        Launcher behavior
39:.agents/      Hidden configuration directory for agent tooling templates/workflows
40:
41:
42:<!-- rtk-instructions v2 -->
43:# RTK (Rust Token Killer) - Token-Optimized Commands
44:
45:## Golden Rule
46:
47:**Always prefix commands with `rtk`**. If RTK has a dedicated filter, it uses it. If not, it passes through unchanged. This means RTK is always safe to use.
48:
49:**Important**: Even in command chains with `&&`, use `rtk`:
50:```bash
51:# ❌ Wrong
52:git add . && git commit -m "msg" && git push
53:
54:# ✅ Correct
55:rtk git add . && rtk git commit -m "msg" && rtk git push
56:```
57:
58:## RTK Commands by Workflow
59:
60:### Build & Compile (80-90% savings)
61:```bash
62:rtk cargo build         # Cargo build output
63:rtk cargo check         # Cargo check output
64:rtk cargo clippy        # Clippy warnings grouped by file (80%)
65:rtk tsc                 # TypeScript errors grouped by file/code (83%)
66:rtk lint                # ESLint/Biome violations grouped (84%)
67:rtk prettier --check    # Files needing format only (70%)
68:rtk next build          # Next.js build with route metrics (87%)
69:```
70:
71:### Test (60-99% savings)
72:```bash
73:rtk cargo test          # Cargo test failures only (90%)
74:rtk go test             # Go test failures only (90%)
75:rtk jest                # Jest failures only (99.5%)
76:rtk vitest              # Vitest failures only (99.5%)
77:rtk playwright test     # Playwright failures only (94%)
78:rtk pytest              # Python test failures only (90%)
79:rtk rake test           # Ruby test failures only (90%)
80:rtk rspec               # RSpec test failures only (60%)
81:rtk test <cmd>          # Generic test wrapper - failures only
82:```
83:
84:### Git (59-80% savings)
85:```bash

# PROJECT KNOWLEDGE BASE

Research monorepo for Intel DSA/IAX data-path work.

## CONVENTIONS

- Keep durable detail in plans, reports, and remarks rather than transient notes.
- Keep commit headlines short and consistent with current style.
- Write commits in focused, reviewable increments, but not so small that they lose a coherent unit of work.
- Write a human project plan in `docs/plan/YYYY-MM-DD/NN.<topic>.<state>.md` before non-trivial project changes. State the goal, scope, intended changes, verification, and completion notes in plain language.
- Always write agent execution/workflow plans in `agents/plan/YYYY-MM-DD/NN.<topic>.<state>.md`.
- Write findings to `docs/report/<topic>/NNN.<descriptor>.<ext>`.
- Write single-point insights to `remark/NNN_<topic>.md`.
- Match code to specs, not specs to code, unless explicitly told otherwise.
- **Code Elegance & Lean Design:** Keep code lean. Do not repeat duplicate logic; abstract if possible, or keep it perfectly clean if unavoidable. If code looks heavyweight with excessive conditionals, stop and design a more elegant approach.
- Keep child `AGENTS.md` files lean and local; do not repeat parent guidance within them.

## DO NOT
- Guess DSA/IAX behavior if `docs/specs/*.md` or `docs/report/architecture/001.design_decisions.md` already cover it.
- Run hardware-facing binaries directly when the documented flow requires `launch` or `dsa_launcher`.

## HARDWARE BATCHING TERMINOLOGY
- Use `hw-eval/` as the hardware potential baseline when comparing accelerator submission strategies.
- Keep `batch` and `concurrency` separate in plans, reports, and code names.
- **Batch size (`batch_n`):** The number of logical operations submitted to hardware through one MMIO submission. Batch size 1 means one operation per MMIO submission.
- **Concurrency:** The maximum number of logical operations outstanding at once, independent of how those operations are grouped into MMIO submissions.
- If a benchmark reports outstanding submission slots instead of logical operations, convert before comparing:
  $$logical\_concurrency = batch\_size \times outstanding\_submission\_slots$$
- Avoid ambiguous phrases like “batch size 1” without specifying whether it means the no-batch/direct-descriptor baseline or a DSA `BATCH` descriptor containing one sub-descriptor.
- Keep hw-eval-specific strategy names and command-line trigger details in `hw-eval/AGENTS.md`.

## REPO MAP
```text
dsa-stdexec/  C++ stdexec sender/receiver framework
accel-rpc/    Rust accelerator-aware RPC workspace
hw-eval/      Hardware potential baseline benchmark harnesses
docs/         Plans, reports, specs, related work
tools/        Launcher behavior
.agents/      Hidden configuration directory for agent tooling templates/workflows

# RTK (Rust Token Killer) - Token-Optimized Commands

## Golden Rule

**Always prefix commands with `rtk`**. If RTK has a dedicated filter, it uses it. If not, it passes through unchanged. This means RTK is always safe to use.

**Important**: Even in command chains with `&&`, use `rtk`:
```bash
# ❌ Wrong
git add . && git commit -m "msg" && git push

# ✅ Correct
rtk git add . && rtk git commit -m "msg" && rtk git push
```

Inherits `../AGENTS.md`.

## CRATE JOB
- Own generic protobuf encoding/decoding behavior, including generated-message async encode hooks.
- Keep `prost::Message::encode_raw` synchronous and CPU-compatible.

- Do not make normal Prost APIs require DSA, Tonic, device paths, or hardware capabilities.
- Hardware-backed DSA tests must stay ignored and opt in through the `hardware-dsa` feature plus `TONIC_DSA_WQ`.

- Keep the raw `Bytes` codec focused on copying payload bytes through DSA without protobuf-specific behavior.

- Generated protobuf field-shape/e2e tests belong in `../prost/tests` and should exercise Prost's async payload-copy hook.

# Prost DSA test ownership
…
## Goal
…

## Scope
- Keep raw bytes DSA codec tests in `tonic-dsa-bytes-async`.
- Place generated protobuf encoding coverage under `prost/tests`.
- Add small crate-local `AGENTS.md` files for `prost/` and `tonic-dsa-bytes-async/`.
- Preserve opt-in hardware execution through the Prost `hardware-dsa` feature, ignored tests, and `TONIC_DSA_WQ`.

## Intended changes
- Remove generated-message shape coverage from the DSA bytes crate hardware test file.
- Add the generated-message DSA e2e hardware coverage to Prost tests.
- Add any test-only dependency wiring needed for Prost tests to drive a DSA-backed async payload sink.
- Keep Tonic codec plumbing unchanged.

## Verification
- Run the targeted Prost async/protobuf encoding tests.
- Run the async DSA crate tests to ensure raw bytes DSA coverage still passes.
- Run the ignored hardware protobuf encoding test through the DSA launcher when direct access is not permitted.

## Completion notes
Completed. Generated protobuf DSA hardware coverage now lives in `prost/tests/src/hardware_dsa.rs` and directly compares Prost async sink encoding against synchronous `prost::Message::encode`; `tonic-dsa-bytes-async/tests/hardware_dsa.rs` keeps only the raw bytes codec hardware smoke test. Added crate-local AGENTS guidance for `prost/` and `tonic-dsa-bytes-async/`. Verified with targeted Prost async encode tests, the ignored DSA protobuf hardware test through `dsa_launcher`, async DSA crate tests, and `git diff --check`.

content.text:
It happened because `hardware_dsa.rs` was only linked from `tests/src/lib.rs` under:

```rust
#[cfg(all(test, feature = "hardware-dsa"))]
mod hardware_dsa;
```

rust-analyzer usually indexes default features, so `hardware-dsa` was inactive. Result: the file existed on disk, but no active crate module pointed at it, so rust-analyzer reported it as “unlinked”.

Fixed by changing the module to always link in test builds:

```rust
#[cfg(test)]
mod hardware_dsa;
```

and moving the feature gate into the file:

```rust
#![cfg(feature = "hardware-dsa")]
```

So rust-analyzer can associate the file with the `tests` crate, while normal builds still do not compile the DSA hardware test unless `--features hardware-dsa` is enabled.

Verified:
```text
cargo test -p tests async_encode
7 passed, 62 filtered out

cargo test -p tests --features hardware-dsa dsa_encode_async_matches_sync_encode_for_generated_payloads -- --nocapture
1 passed

git diff --check
passed
```
